surprises.description: BFST reported GAAP EPS of $0.71, below the preview’s $0.74–$0.75 consensus range, but core EPS was $0.79 after excluding $3.5 million of merger expenses—above both consensus and the preview’s $0.76 estimate. The headline was therefore weaker on a GAAP basis but stronger on underlying profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 GAAP net income was $23.2 million ($0.71 EPS), while core non-GAAP net income was $26 million ($0.79 EPS), excluding $3.5 million in merger-related expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (Q3'26): Consensus $0.74–$0.75”; the preview’s model estimated “Diluted EPS … $0.76.”

surprises.description: Core NIM reached 3.80%, about 8 basis points above the preview’s 3.72% estimate, and management expects further expansion in Q4. That was stronger than the preview’s concern that the hiking-rate backdrop could leave Q4 margin expansion flatter than investors had expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core net interest margin expanded 12 basis points to 3.80%”; management guided to “continued low-to-mid single-digit basis point margin expansion in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “core ~3.72%” and said the risk was that “Q4 NIM guidance comes in flatter than the ‘modest improvement’ cadence the Street extrapolated.”

surprises.description: Deposits rebounded by $141.2 million after the $229 million Q2 decline, rather than shrinking for a second consecutive quarter. The commercial money-market inflows also let BFST reduce brokered deposits and FHLB borrowings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total deposits increased $141.2 million (7.7% annualized), including $180.1 million in commercial money market accounts, enabling paydown of ~$66 million in brokered deposits and $108 million in FHLB borrowings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a second quarter of deposit shrinkage would force funding-cost questions” after deposits fell $229 million in Q2.

surprises.description: Core noninterest expense was $56.9 million, below the approximately $58 million Q3 expectation, as Progressive acquisition savings arrived faster than anticipated. This was a better cost result than the preview’s estimate, not merely the expected step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core noninterest expense fell $1.4 million to $56.9 million due to accelerated Progressive acquisition cost saves.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled core noninterest expense of “$58.0M” and noted management had guided to “~$58M” for Q3.

surprises.description: NPLs declined only modestly to 1.24% of loans, rather than reaching the preview’s expected Q3 range of roughly $67–76 million from $84.1 million. Management described more cleanup ahead, with upwards of $15 million of NPA reductions in Q4 and the 50-basis-point NPL goal framed as a target over time rather than the preview’s approximately $50 million year-end target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonperforming loans decreasing only modestly to 1.24% of loans held for investment”; management expects “NPA reductions of upwards of $15 million in Q4,” targeting an NPL-to-loans ratio of “50 basis points or less over time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “10–20% NPL resolution in Q3” and a “~$50M year-end NPL target,” implying Q3 NPLs of roughly “$67–76M.”

surprises.description: Net charge-offs increased, contrary to the preview’s modeled roughly 9 basis points annualized, but management attributed the increase to one previously identified, fully reserved commercial relationship rather than a new credit migration. The higher charge-offs were a negative result, with the explanation limiting the apparent deterioration in credit quality.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net charge-offs increased during the quarter but were attributable to a single previously identified, fully reserved commercial relationship.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~9bp NCOs annualized” and flagged “any new credit migration” as a threat to the credit-healing narrative.

surprises.description: BFST continued share buybacks even though the preview expected repurchases to be dormant at the current share price, which it put well above management’s stated 120%-of-tangible-book threshold. Tangible book value per share grew only about 1.7% annualized amid AOCI pressure and buybacks, although management said growth would have exceeded 14% without those headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tangible book value per share grew ~1.7% annualized despite AOCI pressure and share buybacks”; management noted it “would have grown over 14% absent those headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that at $31.82, BFST was “well clear of management’s own value threshold” and that “the buyback … is almost certainly switched off.”

surprises.description: Q3 loan discount accretion was about $1.2 million because of higher early paydowns, a temporary earnings and margin support not identified in the preview. Management expects it to fall back to about $500,000 per quarter, so the Q3 contribution is not expected to persist.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loan discount accretion was ~$1.2 million in Q3 due to higher early paydowns but is expected to normalize to about $500,000 per quarter going forward.”

surprises.description: The financial services group disclosed revenue growth of more than 20% annualized and service to over 200 banks, a stronger growth datapoint than the preview’s discussion of APC, SSW, and fee-income durability had anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The financial services group (now serving 200+ banks) is growing revenue over 20% annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed APC’s full-quarter contribution, SSW’s $5.6 billion AUM, and “Fee income durability,” but gave no expectation for financial-services-group revenue growth or bank count.
